preamble: In Faroese, the velar stop /k/ (from Old Norse g) is palatalized to the postalveolar affricate before front vowels and /j/. Because Faroese lenis stops are voiceless and unaspirated, Old Norse [ɡ] before a front vowel now surfaces as [t͡ʃ], which contrasts with aspirated [t͡ʃʰ] from Old Norse k. Icelandic stops at the palatal stop [c] in the same words (gefa [ˈcɛːva]). No other case of plain [ɡ] becoming voiceless [t͡ʃ] has been verified: velar palatalization of [ɡ] elsewhere keeps voicing and gives [d͡ʒ].
